issues.problem: Neither `dropper_bought` nor `conveyor_bought` appears in the counters. The playtest ended after 13s with only about 5 cash, so purchases were never attempted. The 'deduct once' rule and the debounce on the pads (Touched fires many times per touch) are unverified. A double-fire could double-spend or double-buy.
issues.fix_hint: In the pad Touched handler, check `self.bought[kind]` and set it to true BEFORE deducting cost, so repeated touches cannot re-enter. Resolve the touching part to a Player via `Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(hit.Parent)` and accept only the plot owner. Deduct cost only if `cash.Value >= cost`. Call `Telemetry.count` exactly once per successful buy. Send a Notify toast for both success and 'need X cash'. Rate-limit the 'need more cash' toast so it does not spam while the player stands on the pad.

issues.problem: Income is 1 cash every 2s, so the first 25-cash upgrade takes about 50s and the 50-cash one over a minute more. The opening feels slow, and an automated playtest never reaches a purchase, so the buy loop goes untested.
issues.fix_hint: Add a tunable such as STARTING_CASH = 10 (or raise CUBE_VALUE to 2) that Tycoon/Game applies to the leaderstat. Alternatively keep the spec values but add a STARTING_CASH constant so the first buy happens within about 30s. Leave DROP_INTERVAL = 2 as specified.

issues.problem: The HUD shows Cash and a hint line, but there is no per-collection feedback (for example +1 popups) and no indication of upgrade progress or affordability. The 'numbers go up' feeling is weak between purchases.
issues.fix_hint: Tween the cash label (a brief scale pulse or color flash) whenever the value increases. Optionally show the next goal in the hint text, such as 'Next: Dropper 25 (have X)', updated on each Cash change.

iterations.summary: The game runs end to end with no errors or warnings. The map is built, the plot is assigned, cubes drop (7) and are collected (5), and the Cash leaderstat and HUD are wired up. The buy-pad path (`dropper_bought` / `conveyor_bought`) never ran in the playtest, so it is unverified. Early progression is slow, and with a 0.5 cash/s income the first purchase takes about 50 seconds.

issues.problem: The visible header requires only PlotBuilder and Tycoon, never PlazaBuilder or PlotClaimService. It has its own slots/states/teleport/removePlot logic, so players are teleported onto a plot on join. That contradicts the spec: players spawn in the plaza, claim a plot via a gate or the 20s auto-claim, and cubes_dropped stays 0 until then. The counters 'plaza_built', 'themes_built', 'plots_claimed' and 'auto_claims' would likely never fire.
issues.fix_hint: Make Game.server.luau a thin bootstrap. Build the plaza and plots (PlotBuilder plus PlazaBuilder), call PlotClaimService.init with the plot list, and delete the per-player slot assignment and teleport-to-plot code. Spawn players at the plaza (SpawnLocation or PivotTo the plaza center). Start the Tycoon only from PlotClaimService.claim. Bump 'map_built' once.

issues.problem: The claim flow cannot be verified. It relies on defensive fallbacks for the plot table shape (`p.origin or p.spawnCFrame`, `p.gate or p.Gate`), which suggests an unsettled interface with PlotBuilder. It also calls count('plaza_built') here while PlazaBuilder counts it too, so the counter can reach 2 instead of 1.
issues.fix_hint: Define one plot-table shape shared by PlotBuilder and PlotClaimService. Remove the duplicate count('plaza_built') here. Make sure the claim path bumps 'plots_claimed', 'plot_assigned' and 'auto_claims' exactly once per claim, and that the Tycoon starts only after a claim. Guard against the same plot being claimed twice by simultaneous Touched events (check Owner before assigning).

issues.problem: PlotBuilder uses the single Config PLOT_COLOR palette and a SPAWN_LOCAL inside the plot (0,3,12), which fits the old spawn-on-plot flow. The spec requires per-theme floors, decor and no default grey parts, with players spawning in the plaza.
issues.fix_hint: Take each plot's floor material and color plus the rail, dropper and pad colors from PlotThemes. Remove or stop using SPAWN_LOCAL for initial spawn. Keep the buy pads off the path between the gate and the plot center so they are not triggered accidentally.

issues.problem: Cubes are unanchored CanCollide parts moved by the conveyor. With up to 30 cubes per plot across 6 plots they can jitter, stick, or knock players around. Cleanup depends on the cap and a Born attribute, and the collector may double-credit or miss cubes.
issues.fix_hint: Add a lifetime fallback that destroys any cube older than about 30s. Put cubes in a collision group that does not collide with players, or set CanCollide=false. Make the collector idempotent with a per-cube 'collected' attribute check before paying out.

iterations.summary: The playtest did not run (compile check only), so no runtime behaviour or counters are verified. The files compile and the pieces look reasonable (themed PlazaBuilder, PlotClaimService, Tycoon, Hud). However, Game.server.luau appears to wire up the old assign-on-join flow instead of the plaza and claim-gate flow the spec requires.

issues.problem: `themes_built` is 12 but the spec requires exactly 6. Either the theme/plot build runs twice (PlazaBuilder and PlotBuilder both building themes, or the init being called twice) or the counter is bumped twice per theme. Duplicate plots or props at the same ring positions would also explain the 665 instances.
issues.fix_hint: Make sure the plaza and plot ring are built exactly once at startup. Guard the init with a `built` flag, and bump `themes_built` once per theme, not once per builder pass. Confirm there are exactly 6 plot models and 6 gates in Workspace after startup.

issues.problem: The playtest ended at 11.1s with no claim. The player spawns in the plaza and the gates sit on a ring at radius 85 while the plaza radius is 32, so nothing is claimed unless the player walks out. The 20s auto-claim never fired, so the core loop (cubes_dropped, cubes_collected, Cash rising, Dropper 2 purchase) was never exercised.
issues.fix_hint: Check that the auto-claim timer starts at player join (not at character spawn or after the data load) and that it counts 'auto_claims' and 'plot_assigned' when it fires. Optionally move spawn points closer to the nearest gates so a short playtest can reach a claim. Keep the 20s timeout from the spec.

issues.problem: The config still holds old tunables that contradict the spec. `DROPPER_COST = 25` and `CONVEYOR_COST = 50` do not match the first Dropper 2 purchase at 10. The `BOUGHT_COLOR` grey also conflicts with the no-grey-parts rule if it is ever used. Two sources of truth for costs risk the wrong price being used.
issues.fix_hint: Remove the unused legacy cost and colour constants, or set them to the values from `Upgrades.luau`. Make sure no script reads `Config.DROPPER_COST` or `Config.BOUGHT_COLOR` for purchases or pad colouring.

issues.problem: Cash-in feedback has no audio or particle backing: the scene has sounds=0 and particles=0, and cashin_fx_sent never fired. Collecting cubes is silent and static, so the main reward is flat.
issues.fix_hint: On each cube collected, flash the collector part to Color3.fromRGB(255,214,64) and tween it back over 0.15s. Add a ParticleEmitter on the collector and call :Emit(4) on each collect. Fire the client remote with a tier-based pitch. Make sure the client plays a Sound with CASHIN_SOUND_ID at pitchForTier. Throttle to MAX_POPUPS_PER_SECOND. Count cashin_fx_sent.

issues.problem: The sounds are the weak built-in rbxasset wavs ('electronicpingshort.wav', 'button.wav') rather than the verified sound ids in the GameAssets sound table, so cash-in is not a satisfying cha-ching.
issues.fix_hint: Replace CASHIN_SOUND_ID and POP_SOUND_ID with the Coin and Pop ids from the GameAssets sound table. Keep the cash-in volume low (~0.4) and raise the pitch per tier via PITCH_PER_TIER = 0.06 so that rapid cash-ins sound musical and do not spam.

issues.problem: Lighting is set up (atmosphere, bloom, colour correction), but the scene has particles=0, beams=0 and highlights=0, so there is no ambient sparkle. Bloom threshold 1.6 is high, so Neon parts barely glow. The world feels static.
issues.fix_hint: Lower bloom.Threshold to about 1.0 and raise Intensity to 0.8 so Neon pads and gates visibly glow. Make the GameAssets burst helper create and Emit real ParticleEmitters (sparkle texture, gold and theme colours, 20 particles) for purchases and rebirth, and export a helper that attaches a slow ambient sparkle emitter to the plaza fountain.

issues.problem: The tutorial has 4 steps, but tutorial_steps never advanced because nothing was claimed or cashed. The first steps say 'Walk to a CLAIM gate', which conflicts with the auto-claim at 3s, so new players get contradictory guidance.
issues.fix_hint: Start the tutorial at step 2 ('Watch your dropper make cash') when the player is auto-claimed. Fire 'claimed' on auto-claim as well as manual claim, count tutorial_steps on each advance, and play the Pop sound with a sparkle burst on the arrow when a step completes.

issues.problem: The playtest shows data_loaded=1 but no gameplay counters after it, suggesting the load-to-claim handoff may stall (for example waiting for data before claiming). Slow or failed DataStore loads would block fun in Studio.
issues.fix_hint: After a data load or a failed DataStore call (use the memory fallback), immediately fire the same signal that triggers the claim. Use pcall with a 3s timeout and never block the auto-claim on a save/load. Count data_loaded only once.

iterations.summary: The game starts cleanly with no errors or warnings, and the plaza and map are built (`plaza_built` 1, `map_built` 1, 665 instances). The probe never saw the core loop: `plots_claimed`, `plot_assigned`, `cubes_dropped`, `cubes_collected` and `upgrades_bought` are all missing. It ran only 11.1s, which is before the 20s auto-claim, and `themes_built` is 12 instead of 6, so something is built or counted twice.

issues.problem: The runner errors with `ForgeChecks:125: attempt to compare number <= table`, which is the `no_output_errors` branch (`n <= chk.expect...`). In ForgeChecksPlan, `expect` for that check is a table (`{forbidden = {...}, maxAllowed = 0}`), so the number is compared against the table. This kills the runner, leaving 0 checks passed. No claim or auto-claim ever happened, and `plots_claimed`, `plot_assigned`, `cubes_dropped`, `cubes_collected` and `upgrades_bought` are all missing from the counters.
issues.fix_hint: In the `no_output_errors` branch, compare against the numeric field: `record(chk.id, n <= (chk.expect.maxAllowed or 0), ...)`. Also check the other branches for places that use `chk.expect` as a number when the plan supplies a table. Wrap each check in pcall so one bad check cannot abort the run. Make sure the run lasts long enough to cover the 20s auto-claim and the sampling windows.

issues.problem: The `themes_built` counter is 12 but the spec requires exactly 6 for 6 plots. Theme building or its telemetry is probably running twice, for example once per code path or per module require.
issues.fix_hint: Find where `themes_built` is incremented (this module or the server builder that uses it). Count it once per plot theme built, and guard against a second build pass so the total is 6.

issues.problem: CLAIM_TIMEOUT is 20, but the design's first-60-seconds script has the player auto-claimed and dropping cubes by about 3-5s. The playtest saw no auto_claims, plot_assigned or cubes_dropped. A 10-year-old would stand idle on the plaza for 20 seconds.
issues.fix_hint: Set PlotThemes.CLAIM_TIMEOUT = 4 (or 5). Keep the glowing gate and 'Claim <Theme> Plot' billboard so walking onto a gate still claims early. Make sure the auto-claim teleports the player onto the plot and starts the dropper.

issues.problem: themes_built is 12 where 6 is expected. The themes or plots appear to be built twice. This risks duplicate overlapping plots and gates, and the ForgeChecks run already has checks_failed = 1.
issues.fix_hint: Guard the build and the themes_built telemetry increment with a single 'built' flag. Only build from the server (RunService:IsServer()) and never rebuild if Workspace already contains the Plots folder. Increment themes_built once per theme.

issues.problem: The cash-in feedback never ran: cashin_fx_sent is absent, sounds_played is 0 and client_sounds_played is 0. The collector gives no visible or audible reward even though 6 Sound instances exist.
issues.fix_hint: On every collected cube, fire the CashIn remote at least once per 0.25s batch and bump cashin_fx_sent. The client plays the Coin sound from GameAssets with pitch from CashInConfig.pitchForTier, flashes the collector Neon yellow, calls GameAssets burst for a small sparkle, and floats a '+$N' BillboardGui upward with a tween. Confirm the collector fires this path when a cube is destroyed.

issues.problem: The first reward is slow to feel. Cubes are worth 1 and drop every 2s, and STARTING_CASH is 10, while the design wants a +$5 first payout and a Dropper 2 price tag that turns green at about $20. Nothing in the evidence shows a first purchase within 20s.
issues.fix_hint: Raise CUBE_VALUE to 5 (the Bronze ore value) so the first collected cube shows '+$5'. Keep DROP_INTERVAL at 2, or lower it to 1.5 for the first minute. Make sure the Dropper 2 price in Upgrades.luau is reachable within about 15s of claiming.

issues.problem: tutorial_steps stayed at 1. The banner says 'Walk to a CLAIM gate', but the player is meant to be auto-claimed. Step 2 ('Watch your dropper make cash') is never reached, so the player gets no guidance toward the glowing pad.
issues.fix_hint: Change the steps to match the real flow. Step 1 is 'Your plot is ready! Watch the cubes make cash'. Step 2 is 'Step on the glowing green pad to buy Dropper 2'. Step 3 is 'Open the SHOP for more'. Advance step 1 on the CLAIMED event, so tutorial_steps reaches 2 as soon as the plot is claimed. Add a Pop sound and a sparkle burst at each step change.

issues.problem: bursts is 0 and no sound played during the whole playtest, so the game is silent and static. The shared GameAssets helpers (burst, shake, sound) are not being called by the gameplay code.
issues.fix_hint: Wire GameAssets.burst and GameAssets.shake into the buy-pad purchase handler (a gold burst plus a small shake), the dropper nozzle on each drop (a tiny puff), and rebirth (a large burst). Play the verified Buy, Coin, Error and Win sounds through GameAssets at those moments so sounds_played rises above 0.

iterations.summary: The map and plaza build and no runtime errors or warnings appear in the report. The ForgeChecks runner itself crashed at line 125 (`attempt to compare number <= table`), so the playtest ended at about 10s. No claim, drop, collect or buy counters were ever observed, so the core loop is unverified. `themes_built` is 12 where the spec expects 6.

issues.problem: themes_built is 12 but the spec requires exactly 6. The plot/theme build probably runs twice: either the build is called twice at startup, or the counter is bumped twice per theme. This may mean 12 plots or duplicate decor parts.
issues.fix_hint: Make sure PlotBuilder/PlazaBuilder are invoked exactly once at startup. Guard against a second build with a `built` flag, and bump themes_built once per theme (6 total). Check that the Workspace holds only 6 plot models.

issues.problem: plots_claimed = 2 and auto_claims = 2 with a single player, while plot_assigned = 1. Auto-claim fired within 6.5s of uptime, well before the 20s timeout. Two timers appear to exist (PlotClaimService's own and the fallback timer here), and both counted a claim. The player may have been claimed twice, or the second claim leaked.
issues.fix_hint: Make the claim path idempotent. In the fallback timer, return early if hasClaimedPlot(player) or the player already owns a plot, and do not bump auto_claims or plots_claimed a second time. Keep only one authority for auto-claim (PlotClaimService), and make sure the delay is 20s and not shortened.

issues.problem: Players spawn in the plaza, but the plaza teleport is conditional on hasClaimedPlot, and cubes_dropped is already 2 at 6.5s. It is unclear whether the player ever stood in the plaza or walked onto a gate, since auto-claim happened implicitly. The tutorial and claim-by-walking acceptance criteria are unverified.
issues.fix_hint: Only start the dropper after a real claim, and make sure nothing claims the plot until a gate touch or the 20s timeout. Verify the character is moved to the plaza center on CharacterAdded and not teleported again on respawn after a claim.

issues.problem: No cashin_fx_sent or cubes_collected counter ever fired, so the first-reward moment (flash, +$N, Coin) never happens. sounds_played and client_sounds_played are both 0 even though 6 server sounds and 7 client sounds exist.
issues.fix_hint: Where cubes are paid out, always call ForgeTelemetry.count('cashin_fx_sent') and fire the CashIn remote to the owner immediately for the first few cubes, then batch. Make sure the collector part is the one whose Touched or poll triggers the payout. Play the Coin sound from GameAssets on the collector at tier pitch, flash the collector Neon yellow with a TweenService tween, and call GameAssets.burst at the intake.

issues.problem: The census shows bursts is 0 and sounds_played is 0. The helper functions exist but nothing triggers them, and the ambient sparkle is the only particle use.
issues.fix_hint: Make GameAssets.sound(name, parent) always create the Sound and call :Play(), and add a Debris cleanup. Make sure GameAssets.burst(at, color, count) is called from the dropper on each drop (count 4, tiny puff) and from the pad on purchase (count 30).

issues.problem: The first buy relies on early income, but cubes_collected never rose, so Dropper 2 cannot be afforded. The tutorial is stuck at step 1 and nobody gets guided to the pad.
issues.fix_hint: Raise the starter cash so the first upgrade is affordable at once (the upgrades are priced from $10). Alternatively set the first cube value to 5 so the first pad is affordable at about 10 s, matching the director's '+$5' beat.

issues.problem: The tutorial is stuck at tutorial_steps 1, and the events CASHED and BOUGHT never fire. The player gets no direction after the plot is claimed.
issues.fix_hint: Advance step 2 on the CLAIMED event after about 3 s without waiting for cash. Change step 3's banner text to 'Step on the glowing GREEN pad: $10' and keep the arrow bouncing over the pad. Add a Pop sound on each step.

issues.problem: themes_built is 12 rather than 6, so themes and plots are likely built twice. That could mean duplicate gates and signs, and it adds clutter. plots_claimed is 2 with plot_assigned 1.
issues.fix_hint: Guard the theme builder with an idempotent check, such as skipping a plot if workspace.Plots:FindFirstChild(theme.name) exists. Count themes_built once per theme.

iterations.summary: The playtest ran with no errors or warnings. The plaza, themes, plot claim and dropper all started: map_built, plaza_built, plot_assigned and cubes_dropped (2) are present. But the counters look duplicated (themes_built is 12 instead of 6, and plots_claimed and auto_claims are 2 for one player). The run was too short (6.5s) to show collection, cash growth or purchases.

issues.problem: 'cubes_collected' is missing from the counters, and so are 'upgrades_bought', 'dropper_bought' and 'conveyor_bought'. Two cubes dropped, but none was seen reaching the collector and adding Cash. The playtest ended at 6.4s, so the cause could be the short run or a broken collector path. With a 24-stud conveyor at speed 8 a cube needs about 3s plus spawn time, so this is borderline.
issues.fix_hint: Check that the collector Touched or region handler runs for cubes from the first drop. It should increment the Cash leaderstat, call ForgeTelemetry.count('cubes_collected'), and destroy the cube. Make sure the collector is positioned and sized so a cube cannot slide past it. Consider spawning the first cube immediately on claim, so the first collect happens within about 4s.

issues.problem: The header comments and the data contradict the spec and Config. They say Dropper 2 = 25, Speed 1 = 50 and starterCash = 25, and describe Bronze as worth 5 cash. The spec requires the first purchase (Dropper 2) to cost 10, Config.STARTING_CASH is 10, and the cube value is 1. The shown portion is inconsistent, and the actual cost could not be verified.
issues.fix_hint: Make the file the single source of truth. Set Dropper2 cost to 10 and starterCash to 10, or remove the field and read Config.STARTING_CASH. Fix the stale comments and ore values so the first pad is affordable about 10s after claiming, and verify there are 10 upgrades with unique ids.

issues.problem: The census shows sounds_played 0, client_sounds_played 0 and bursts 0. No cash-in or purchase feedback (sound, sparkle) fired during the playtest. This is probably because no cube was collected, but it is unconfirmed.
issues.fix_hint: Make sure the collector flash, burst and Coin sound fire on every collect. Fire the PurchaseFx remote on purchase. Count 'juice_events' on each collect so the feedback is verifiable.

issues.problem: No cash-in feedback fired in the playtest. Counters show cubes_collected and cashin_fx_sent absent, juice_events=1, sounds_played=0 and bursts=0. The core reward moment, the first cube paying out, is silent and invisible.
issues.fix_hint: Fire the cash-in remote on every collected cube, or in a short batch (~0.25s), with the amount, tier colour and collector position. Increment ForgeTelemetry 'cashin_fx_sent'. The client should play the Coin sound with pitch from CashInConfig.pitchForTier, flash the collector yellow with a Neon tween, call GameAssets.burst at the intake, and float a '+$N' BillboardGui upward over the collector.

issues.problem: The purchase feedback path has no evidence of running (upgrades_bought absent, no PurchaseFx). Buying Dropper 2 is the first meaningful decision and needs to feel big.
issues.fix_hint: On a successful buy, fire PurchaseFx with the upgrade name and position. The client plays the Buy sound, pops the pad (tween Size to 0 with a Back easing), calls GameAssets.burst with the theme glow colour (count ~30), shakes the camera slightly, and shows the toast 'Unlocked: Dropper 2!'. On failure, flash the pad red, play the Error sound and show the toast 'Need $X more'.

issues.problem: The header comments and starterCash=25 disagree with the other files. Config.STARTING_CASH is 10 and the tutorial text says the pad costs $10, while the Upgrades comments say Dropper 2 costs 25. If the cost and starter cash disagree, the first buy may not be reachable in the first 20 seconds. The playtest never reached a buy.
issues.fix_hint: Make the data consistent. Set Dropper 2 cost to 10 and starterCash to 10 (or 0 with the 5-cash Bronze cubes), update the comments, and make sure the tutorial banner and pad billboard read the same price from this table. The pad should be affordable about 10 seconds after claiming.

issues.problem: The tutorial only reached step 1 (tutorial_steps=1). The steps depend on server events (cashed, bought) that never happened, so the player is left with no guidance after claiming.
issues.fix_hint: Add a timed fallback so the banner advances from step 2 ('Watch your dropper make cash') to step 3 ('Step on the glowing GREEN pad: $10') after about 8 seconds even without a cash event. Keep the bobbing arrow and beam pointed at the Dropper 2 pad, and play the Pop sound with a sparkle on each step advance.

issues.problem: Sound resolution is dynamic (GameAssets lookup with a fallback) and 6 client sounds exist, but sounds_played=0 on both server and client. Either the lookups are failing silently or nothing triggers playback.
issues.fix_hint: Make resolveSound fall back to the verified GameAssets.Sounds ids for Coin, Buy, Error, Win and Pop when the lookup returns nil, and print a warn on failure. Make sure the client handler calls :Play() on the Sound for every event, with PlaybackSpeed set from pitchForTier.

iterations.summary: The playtest ran cleanly with no errors or warnings. The plaza, 6 themes and map were built, and a plot was auto-claimed and cubes started dropping (cubes_dropped 2). However, the run lasted only 6.4s, so the collect, cash, purchase and feedback parts of the loop never showed up in the counters.

issues.problem: The playtest only covered the auto-claim path (auto_claims=1, plots_claimed=1). Claiming a plot by walking onto a gate, with the sign showing the player's name and the gate hiding, was never verified. ForgeChecksPlan.claimMode is 'auto', so a bug in gate touch handling would go unnoticed. The only evidence is the plots_claimed counter, which does not show whether the gate and sign state are correct.
issues.fix_hint: Make sure the gate Touched handler checks that the toucher is a player character, has a per-player debounce, and rejects plots that are already claimed. After claiming, set the sign text to the player's name, hide the gate (Transparency=1, CanTouch=false, billboard disabled), and count 'plots_claimed' and 'plot_assigned' once. Consider switching ForgeChecksPlan.claimMode to 'gate' in a later playtest.

issues.problem: The census shows 'bursts': 0 and 'sounds_played': 0 on the server, while the counters show bursts=26 and sounds_played=26. Client-side census has client_sounds_played 0 too. The cash-in sound and burst may not actually be playing or may be cleaned up before they are counted, so the counters may be inflated without any real audio or visual feedback.
issues.fix_hint: Verify that the cash-in Sound has a valid SoundId and is parented somewhere that can play it (collector part or SoundService). Call :Play() after it is parented and count 'sounds_played' only after Play succeeds. Check that the burst emitter lives long enough, via Debris or Emit, to be visible, and confirm on the client that the PurchaseFx/CashIn remote handlers actually call Play.

issues.problem: The duplicate-startup guard calls warn() and returns if ForgeWorldBuilt is already set. The spec requires no warnings in the output. A Studio script re-run or a duplicate copy of the script would produce a warning and fail the no_output_errors check.
issues.fix_hint: Replace the warn() with a silent return or a print, or use a ForgeTelemetry counter instead, so a benign duplicate start does not add a warning to the output.

issues.problem: The playtest fell back to an in-memory store ('DataService: using in-memory store'), so the real DataStore save/load path was not exercised. Yielding DataStore calls with retries could stall player setup or leak progress on leave in a live server.
issues.fix_hint: Make sure every DataStore call is wrapped in pcall with a timeout, that PlayerRemoving and BindToClose save once without double-saving, and that the player's setup (leaderstats, plot claim) never waits on a load longer than LOAD_TIMEOUT, falling back to defaults.

issues.problem: Early pacing is too slow. Cubes pay 1 cash each every 2s, Dropper 2 uses the starter $10, and Speed 1 costs 50. After Dropper 2 the player earns about 1 cash/s, so they wait roughly 50s of idle watching. The playtest never opened the shop or bought a second upgrade, and the design doc expects $5 per cube and a $45 Speed 1.
issues.fix_hint: Raise the Bronze ore value from 1 to 5, or the base cube value, so the first cube pays +$5. Lower Speed 1 (Fast Belt) to about 30-45 so it is affordable around t=35-40s. Keep Dropper 2 at 10 and keep the costs in this file only.

issues.problem: The census reports sounds_played=0 on both the server and client sides, and 0 highlights. Purchases and cash-ins may be visually busy but audio-quiet, and there is no affordable-pad glow or error feedback.
issues.fix_hint: On each collected cube, fire the client the tier colour and pitch from CashInConfig.pitchForTier(tier) and play the Coin tick from the GameAssets sound table. On purchase, play the Buy chime and, for ore tiers, the Win sting. On a failed purchase, send an 'error' payload so the client plays the Error buzz and flashes the pad red.

issues.problem: Big moments (upgrade, ore tier, multiplier) have no evidenced camera shake or FOV punch. The purchase FX counter is 1, but nothing shows a shockwave ring or a large reward popup.
issues.fix_hint: Extend the PurchaseFx payload with a 'magnitude' field (1 for a normal buy, 2 for an ore tier or multiplier). Have the client apply a GameAssets camera shake scaled by magnitude plus a +8 FOV tween that returns over 0.25s. Spawn an expanding Neon ring in the tier colour at the dropper, and show a RewardPopup such as 'GOLD ORE! $N per cube'.

issues.problem: The tutorial reached step 2 but never led the player to the shop (no shop_opened). The census shows 0 beams, so the player-to-target guide beam that BEAM_COLOR and BEAM_WIDTH describe is not appearing. Step text 4 is also easy to miss.
issues.fix_hint: Reword STEPS[4] to 'Tap the yellow SHOP button, buy Fast Belt!'. Raise BEAM_WIDTH to about 1 and ARROW_HEIGHT slightly so the guide is more visible. Add a short SHOP_NUDGE_SECONDS (about 8) value that the tutorial client uses to pulse the SHOP button if the shop has not been opened.

iterations.summary: The game runs end to end with no errors or warnings. All 11 ForgeChecks pass: the map, plaza and 6 themes are built, the plot is auto-claimed, cubes drop and are collected, cash rises, and a Dropper 2 purchase goes through once (dropper_bought and upgrades_bought are both 1). Feedback and polish systems (FX, sounds, tutorial, HUD, shop, rebirth) are all active. The remaining gaps are that the playtest never exercised gate claiming or the later upgrades, and some polish counters look inconsistent.

issues.problem: The report has no `upgrades_bought` counter, no shop counters and no purchase telemetry. The core progression (touch the Dropper 2 pad, spend 10, reveal the next pads) never happened in the 32s playtest. Starting cash is 10, so the pad was affordable, but nothing shows the touch path works or that a pad is only reachable by deliberate walking. The checkClaim and onPlotClaimed handoff to UpgradeService also hides failures behind callFirst, which silently skips a missing method.
issues.fix_hint: Make callFirst log a one-time warning if none of the named methods exist, so a broken UpgradeService hookup is visible. Make sure the ForgeTest harness walks to the Dropper 2 pad after claiming so that `upgrades_bought` is exercised.

issues.problem: Config.CUBE_VALUE = 1 conflicts with Upgrades.luau, which says the first (Bronze) cube pays 5 and uses a per-ore value table. Two sources of truth for cube value risk the HUD, tutorial or collector reading the wrong number. The spec's core loop says 1-cash cubes. The header comment also claims prices live only in Upgrades.luau.
issues.fix_hint: Remove CUBE_VALUE from Config, or set it to the real base value and have the dropper and collector read it. Add a comment that ore values come from Upgrades.ores. Check that the tutorial text and HUD income display use the same number.

issues.problem: Cash-in feedback is rate-limited per player (allowSend, about 8 per second) and the code depends on TutorialService being present. Telemetry shows 13 `cashin_fx_sent` for 13 collected cubes, so it works now. With many droppers late in the game, popups may be dropped and the feedback will look inconsistent.
issues.fix_hint: Instead of dropping popups over the limit, aggregate them into one popup that sums the values. Wrap the TutorialService require in a guarded pcall-style lookup so a missing module can't stop this service.

issues.problem: The ForgeWorldBuilt guard returns silently on a second run. If the script is ever duplicated or restarted in Studio, the world and services never start, and nothing in the output says why.
issues.fix_hint: Keep the single-start guard but add a `ForgeTelemetry.count("duplicate_start")` or a debug-level print before returning, so it can be diagnosed without raising a warning.

issues.problem: The first purchase never happened in the playtest. The player starts with exactly $10, which is the Dropper 2 price, yet upgrades_bought is absent. Either the pad is hard to find or reach, or nothing guides the player to it.
issues.fix_hint: After a plot is claimed, make sure the Dropper 2 pad is set to the theme accent colour with a Neon pulse, and tell the tutorial to point at it. Re-check that the pad's Touched hitbox is large enough (about 8x1x8) and is not blocked by the conveyor or the spawn path. Fire the tutorial CLAIMED event right after the claim so the guide beam appears.

issues.problem: The census shows beams=0 and highlights=0, so the guide to the first pad is probably invisible. The config defines BEAM_COLOR and BEAM_WIDTH, but no beam was present in the scene.
issues.fix_hint: Raise BEAM_WIDTH to about 1.5 and use a bright BEAM_COLOR (255,240,120). Keep the beam alive until upgrades_bought>=1. Add a Highlight (FillColor green, OutlineColor white) on the target pad so it is visible from across the plot.

issues.problem: Cash-in feedback is the same for every cube, so there are no big moments. There is no milestone feedback for the first cube, for reaching affordability or for income milestones, and the first reward is not special.
issues.fix_hint: Add a larger celebration at milestones. For the very first collected cube, and at cumulative collected counts of 10, 50 and 100, fire GameAssets.burst(collector, tierColor, 30) and send a larger +$ popup with 1.5x text size and a Win sound. Raise the pitch for combo streaks using CashInConfig.pitchForTier.

issues.problem: The first spend is gated only by starter cash (10), which is spent instantly with no waiting. A new player has no chase and may buy before understanding cubes. Tier-up value jumps (Gold 30, Diamond 75) have no big payoff presentation to anchor them.
issues.fix_hint: Keep Dropper 2 at 10 but add a `label` and `popup` string to each ore upgrade (for example 'GOLD ORE! $30 per cube') so the client can show a RewardPopup with a Win sting, a shockwave ring and an FOV punch when the tier is bought. Check that each upgrade requires an existing id so the pads reveal progressively.

iterations.summary: The game runs cleanly with no errors or warnings. The plaza, 6 themed plots, claim gate and auto-claim all work, cubes drop and are collected (15 dropped, 13 collected), and the HUD, tutorial, juice and leaderboard systems are all active. The buy-pad flow was never exercised in the playtest (no upgrades_bought, dropper_bought or conveyor_bought counter), so the main progression loop is unverified.

issues.problem: The console prints `[Forge] no method found for: init/start/setup` and `no method found for: onPlotClaimed` and `onPlotClaimed/onClaimed`. The script calls optional hooks on services without checking that they exist and logs the miss. The acceptance criteria want a clean output, and the lines suggest the plot-claim event may not reach the service meant to react to it (for example the tutorial or the upgrade pads). Claiming still works, because `plots_claimed` and `plot_assigned` are 1.
issues.fix_hint: Find which service each missing method was meant for and make sure its claim hook actually exists and is called. Drop the print for optional hooks that are intentionally absent, or gate it behind a debug flag, so the output stays quiet.

issues.problem: The report has no `upgrades_bought`, `dropper_bought` or `conveyor_bought` counter. Only `pad_highlighted` is 1, so the main purchase beat never happened. The player auto-claimed with 10 starting cash and never bought Dropper 2, so the pad reveal chain (Silver, Speed 1, Dropper 3), the exactly-once deduction and the insufficient-cash denial are unverified.
issues.fix_hint: Make sure the Dropper 2 pad is reachable and placed just off the player's walking path. Verify that a Touched event from the character's HumanoidRootPart reaches the purchase handler. Add a ForgeTest hook or auto-buy path so the playtest can exercise the first purchase, and confirm that `upgrades_bought` increments exactly once.

issues.problem: Sounds are effectively silent. The census shows sounds_played=0 and client_sounds_played=0 even though the counter sounds_played is 15, and the sound is a per-part Sound parented to the collector with Volume 0.5 and a SoundId from config. It may be failing to load, or it is too quiet and only server-side, so the main reward (cha-ching) is not audible.
issues.fix_hint: Send the cash-in event to the client, which plays a 2D Sound in SoundService using the verified coin sound id from GameAssets sounds. Set Volume to 0.8 and PlaybackSpeed from pitchForTier, and use SoundService:PlayLocalSound or a Sound with Parent=SoundService. Keep the server Sound only as a fallback. Count client_sounds_played.

issues.problem: The player never bought anything in the playtest (no upgrades_bought), so the core hook of spending cash is unproven. The Dropper 2 pad may be too hard to find or reach. tutorial_reshown=1 suggests the player got stuck on a step.
issues.fix_hint: Make the Dropper 2 pad larger (about 6x1x6), place it 10-12 studs in front of the spawn point on the plot, and add a pulsing Neon glow and a bobbing arrow BillboardGui reading 'Step here! $10'. Keep STARTING_CASH at 10 so it is affordable at claim, and let touch trigger the buy at once.

issues.problem: The census reports bursts=0 and particles=8 against 26 bursts counted, so burst emitters are short-lived and possibly too small to notice. Collection and purchase sparkle needs to be bigger and more visible.
issues.fix_hint: In GameAssets.burst, raise the default count to 20-30, set the particle Size NumberSequence to 0.6->0, Speed 12-20, Lifetime 0.6-1.0, LightEmission 1 and a gold/theme ColorSequence. Add a ring or confetti variant (Neon part tweened scale 1->8 with Transparency 0->1 over 0.4s) for upgrade and rebirth.

issues.problem: The cash-in reward is not escalating. The collector flash, floating +$N and HUD punch exist in counters (cashin_fx_sent=13), but there is no evidence of the big-moment layers, and cashin_milestones=2 is the only escalation.
issues.fix_hint: Fire a bigger milestone effect at cash thresholds ($50, $100, $500...). Show a RewardPopup 'MILESTONE $100!' with a Back-tween scale, a Win sound and a camera shake. Also make the +$N text larger and the colour match the tier (CashInConfig.colorForTier).

issues.problem: The tutorial stalled (tutorial_reshown=1) and the player progressed through only some steps. A 10-year-old needs a clearer objective from second 0.
issues.fix_hint: Reduce STUCK_RESHOW_SECONDS from 15 to 8. Make the banner text one short command per step, such as 'Collect $10 from cubes!' then 'Step on the glowing green pad!', and keep the beam to the target on at all times.

issues.problem: There is no evidence of the shop, rebirth, error buzz or purchase-failure feedback, since shop_opened, shop_purchases and rebirths never appeared in the counters. A player who cannot afford a pad gets no feedback, which is confusing.
issues.fix_hint: When a pad is touched with too little cash, call the notify remote with 'Need $X more', play the Error sound on the client, flash the pad Color3.fromRGB(255,70,70) for 0.2s and shake the price BillboardGui by tweening its StudsOffset. Debounce this per player at 1.5s so it does not spam.

iterations.summary: The game runs end to end with no errors or warnings. The plaza and 6 themed plots are built, the player is auto-claimed onto a plot, cubes drop and are collected (14 dropped, 13 collected), and the HUD, juice, tutorial, leaderboard and data services all fire. The purchase path never ran in the playtest, so `upgrades_bought` never appears. The console also shows noisy `[Forge] no method found` lines.

issues.problem: The counters show no purchase activity: `upgrades_bought`, `dropper_bought`, `conveyor_bought` and any purchase-FX counter are absent. The 12 checks cover claim, drops, collection and cash, but not the acceptance criteria for buying Dropper 2 exactly once, the pad vanishing, the next three pads appearing, or an insufficient-cash touch doing nothing. The spec's central progression loop was therefore not shown to work.
issues.fix_hint: Add checks that run after claim and cash >= 10. Teleport the character onto the Dropper 2 pad, then assert that `upgrades_bought` == 1, Cash dropped by exactly 10 plus any income, and the pad is hidden. Touch it again and assert the count does not change. Also touch a pad with insufficient cash and assert nothing changes.

issues.problem: Comments and values disagree with the spec and with each other. The comment says the cube value is a fallback and Bronze pays 5, while the spec says a 1-cash cube. `Upgrades.luau` says Speed 1 costs 22, which may differ from the original 50-cash design. Starting cash is 10, so Dropper 2 is affordable immediately, which weakens the 'cash reaches 10 within ~10s' criterion. This is a design risk, not a bug.
issues.fix_hint: Confirm that the economy values match the final spec (cube value, starter cash, Dropper 2 = 10, Speed 1 cost). Keep the comments consistent, and consider starting cash at 0 so the player earns the first purchase.

issues.problem: A `Sound` is created and parented to the PlayerGui for every cash-in (`cashin_local_sounds` = 15, `sounds_played` = 15, `bursts` = 26 for 13 collected cubes). This is a lot of audio and particle churn for a cube every 2s, and it will get louder and more crowded as droppers are added.
issues.fix_hint: Throttle cash-in sound and burst per player, for example at most one every 0.15s, or batch values. Make sure every Sound is destroyed after it plays through Debris or `Ended`.

issues.problem: The duplicate-start guard returns silently apart from a telemetry bump. This is fine, but the file is very large (about 30K characters were truncated from view). It owns the world build, claiming and auto-claim, which makes later changes risky.
issues.fix_hint: Move the plot-claim and auto-claim logic into its own module. Keep Game.server.luau as a thin bootstrap that starts the services in order.

issues.problem: starterCash is 10 and Dropper 2 costs 10, so the first pad is affordable at second 0. The player gets no earn-then-spend moment from the first collected cube. The playtest never recorded a purchase at all.
issues.fix_hint: Set starterCash to 0 (and keep Config.STARTING_CASH in sync) so the first two $5 cubes visibly fill the HUD goal bar before the Dropper 2 pad turns green. If playtest pacing needs it, set starterCash to 5. Keep Dropper 2 at cost 10 so the spec still holds.

issues.problem: tutorial_reshown=3 means the player sat stuck on a step several times, and the census shows beams=0, so no guide beam appears. Players may not find the pad.
issues.fix_hint: Lower STUCK_RESHOW_SECONDS from 8 to 5. Raise BEAM_WIDTH to about 2 and keep the bright yellow BEAM_COLOR (255,240,120) so the guide line to the Dropper 2 pad is obvious. Lower SHOP_STEP_FALLBACK_SECONDS to about 12 so the guide never stalls.

issues.problem: Cash-in feedback works (13 FX sent, sounds played), but the evidence shows no purchase feedback at all (no purchase counter), so the biggest reward moment looks missing.
issues.fix_hint: On every successful purchase, fire the PurchaseFx remote with the pad position and tier colour. The client should play the Buy chime, spawn a sparkle burst (ParticleEmitter:Emit(30)) and punch the cash label. Also increment a 'purchase_fx_sent' counter. On a rejected buy, send an Error buzz plus a 'Need $X more' toast payload.

issues.problem: Cash-in sounds scale pitch per tier, but nothing marks bigger moments (cashin_milestones=2) differently from a normal tick. Collecting feels the same at $5 and at $500.
issues.fix_hint: Add milestone tunables: MILESTONE_SCALE ~1.6 for the +$ popup size, a gold flash colour, and a second layered Win sound at a lower volume. The service and client should use these when a milestone fires, so milestones feel bigger than normal ticks.

iterations.summary: The game runs end to end with no errors or warnings. All 12 ForgeChecks pass: the plaza, 6 themes and map build once, no cubes drop before a claim, and auto-claim fires. After the claim, cubes drop and are collected (15 and 13), Cash rises, and the cash-in FX, tutorial, leaderboard and data service all report activity. The playtest never exercised a pad purchase, so the core upgrade loop is unverified.

issues.problem: The counters show no 'upgrades_bought' (and no 'dropper_bought' or 'conveyor_bought'), although 'pad_highlighted' is 1, so the Dropper 2 pad became affordable. The purchase flow (deduct 10 once, pad vanishes, next pads appear) never ran, so those acceptance criteria are unverified. Also, 15 cubes dropped in a 32.5s run where 'auto_claims' is 1 (claim at roughly 20s) is more than a 2s cadence would give, so the drop timing is suspicious.
issues.fix_hint: Make sure a successful purchase calls ForgeTelemetry.bump('upgrades_bought') exactly once, after the cost is deducted. Make the ForgeTest/probe walk the character onto the Dropper 2 pad once Cash >= 10 so the counter is exercised. Check that the dropper loop starts only after the plot is claimed and uses a 2s interval, so cubes_dropped matches the spec.

issues.problem: The playtest never bought anything (no upgrades_bought or dropper_bought). The Dropper 2 pad is likely off the player's route after the claim teleport, so the main reward moment is never reached.
issues.fix_hint: After a claim, teleport the player to a spot facing the conveyor and within about 12 studs of the Dropper 2 pad. Keep the pad off the direct spawn line so it is not triggered by accident. Give it a Neon accent glow and a PointLight so it is the brightest thing nearby.

issues.problem: CLAIM_TIMEOUT = 20 means a new player waits up to 20s in the plaza with nothing earning. The design doc wants the claim at about 3s and the first cash at about 8s.
issues.fix_hint: Set CLAIM_TIMEOUT to 5. Add a countdown line to the gate BillboardGui, such as 'Claim Candy Plot - auto in 3...', so a 10-year-old sees what is about to happen.

issues.problem: Census beams=0 and tutorial_reshown=1: the guidance beam or arrow was not visible and the step stalled. Nothing visibly guides the player to the $10 pad.
issues.fix_hint: Lower STUCK_RESHOW_SECONDS from 5 to 3. Keep the BEAM_COLOR beam attached to the current target (the Dropper 2 pad first) for the whole step. Add a bobbing arrow above the pad that stays until upgrades_bought >= 1.

issues.problem: Cash-in feedback is the same for every cube, and only 2 milestones fired in 13 collects. Nothing escalates, so the loop flattens after the first few cubes.
issues.fix_hint: Fire a bigger effect every 10th cube: a gold sparkle burst at the collector plus a rising-pitch tick using milestonePitchForTier. Make the floating +$N bigger and gold on milestones, and flash the collector Neon yellow for 0.1s on every collect.

issues.problem: The playtest shows no purchase progression, and the first 60 seconds should chain buys. The price curve after Dropper 2 (10) and Speed 1 (22) may leave long dead gaps with nothing to chase.
issues.fix_hint: Keep the first four purchases at $10, $22, about $40 and about $75, so one purchase lands roughly every 10-15s. Make sure each upgrade has a distinct visible effect (a new dropper model, an ore colour change with sparkles=true) so every buy changes the look of the plot.

issues.problem: The rebirth cost (baseCost 5000) is lower than the design doc's roughly $25k, and with costGrowth 2 the long-term chase is short. After the 10 upgrades there is little to chase.
issues.fix_hint: Raise baseCost to 20000, keep costGrowth at 2 and multPerRebirth at 0.5. Show 'Rebirth at $20K' on the HUD goal bar so players have a visible end target.

iterations.summary: The game starts cleanly with no errors or warnings. The plaza, 6 themed plots, plot claim (via auto-claim), dropping, collecting and cash-in feedback all happened: map_built, plaza_built, themes_built=6, plot_assigned, cubes_dropped=15 and cubes_collected=13. The purchase path was never exercised in the playtest, so upgrades_bought is missing. Several acceptance criteria therefore remain unverified.

issues.problem: The report has no 'upgrades_bought', 'dropper_bought' or 'conveyor_bought' counters, and the tutorial reached only 2 steps in 32s. The purchase loop (Dropper 2 for 10, the pad vanishing, the next pads appearing) was never exercised, so it is untested. The 13 collected cubes should have been enough cash to buy it.
issues.fix_hint: Confirm that the pad touch handler fires for a character standing on the pad. When cash >= cost, deduct it once and bump 'upgrades_bought'. Check that the Dropper 2 pad turns the accent color once cash reaches 10 (the 'pad_highlighted' counter is 1, so this may be working). Consider having the ForgeTest path walk onto the pad so the purchase is verified.

issues.problem: The player was auto-claimed ('auto_claims' 1) and 'plots_claimed' is 1, but the playtest does not show whether gate-touch claiming works. The auto-claim may just be masking a gate that the player cannot reach or trigger.
issues.fix_hint: Verify that the gate's Touched handler is connected on a part with CanTouch enabled, and that the gate sits on the plaza side of the plot where the player can walk onto it. Count a manual claim and an auto-claim separately so a test can tell them apart.

issues.problem: The player never bought Dropper 2 in the playtest (no upgrades_bought) even though 13 cubes were collected, which at $5 each is enough for the $10 pad. The pad path or its touch trigger is not drawing the player in, so the key first-purchase beat is missing.
issues.fix_hint: Place the Dropper 2 pad close to the conveyor path, about 8 studs from the collector or spawn teleport and visible from the claim point. Make its Touched hitbox a larger invisible part (about 8x2x8). Once cash >= cost, auto-trigger the purchase when the player is within about 6 studs, or make the pad pulse Neon green. Increment upgrades_bought on purchase.

issues.problem: The economy pacing depends on slow, small steps, with Dropper 2 at $10 and Speed 1 at $22. Thirteen collected cubes in the session and no purchase suggest income feels slow with no obvious next target.
issues.fix_hint: Lower early pacing: give the first Bronze cube value 5 and a collector burst every cube, and keep Dropper 2 at $10. Make Speed 1 cost about $20 and Dropper 3 about $40 so a purchase lands roughly every 8-10s in the first minute. Add a short 'x2 cash for 60 seconds' welcome boost if the first buy is not made within 20s.

issues.problem: The census shows sounds_played=0 and client_sounds_played=0 even though the counters report sounds_played=15. Audio may be routed through a path the census cannot see, so the cube-collect and buy sounds are uncertain. Particle bursts also read as 0 in the census while 26 were counted.
issues.fix_hint: Make GameAssets.sound parent each Sound to workspace or SoundService, set Volume to at least 0.6, and call Play after the Sound is parented. Confirm the SoundId values are from the verified sound table. Create a few persistent ParticleEmitters (collector sparkle, dropper puff) in the world, not only transient bursts, so they appear in the census.

issues.problem: Cash-in feedback fires for every cube with the same flash, with only 2 milestones. Nothing escalates, so the collect moment becomes wallpaper after 10 cubes.
issues.fix_hint: Scale the feedback with the cube value and a combo count. Raise the pitch a little per consecutive cube within 3s using CashInConfig.pitchForTier. Add a bigger gold sparkle and a larger '+$N' text at every 10th cube, and a short collector Neon pulse tween (Size 1.0 to 1.15 and back, 0.15s).

issues.problem: The tutorial hint was reshown (tutorial_reshown=1) and the arrow advanced only 2 steps in the playtest, so the player was probably unsure where to go to spend their first cash.
issues.fix_hint: Reduce STUCK_RESHOW_SECONDS from 5 to 3 for the buy step. Make the beam from the player to the Dropper 2 pad thicker (BEAM_WIDTH 3) and bright yellow. Add a banner text such as 'Step on the glowing pad to buy Dropper 2 ($10)' once cash >= 10.

issues.problem: The HUD and shop UI share a cream and yellow kit, but there is no evidence of animated feedback on the cash counter or a visible goal bar, so the 'next goal' is not obvious at a glance.
issues.fix_hint: Add a UiTheme.punch(guiObject) helper that tweens Size/Scale to 1.15 then back with Back easing in 0.18s, and call it on every cash change. Add a 'Next: Dropper 2 $10' progress bar under the cash counter that fills green as cash approaches the cost and flashes when affordable.

iterations.summary: The playtest ran clean with no errors or warnings. The plaza and all 6 themed plots were built, the player was auto-claimed, and cubes dropped and were collected (15 dropped, 13 collected). The cash-in, juice, tutorial, and leaderboard systems all fired. The one visible gap is that no purchase counters appear, so buying was never confirmed in this run.

issues.problem: No purchase counters (`upgrades_bought`, `dropper_bought`, `conveyor_bought`) appear in the report, even though 13 cubes were collected and the player should have had at least 10 cash. `pad_highlighted` is 1, so the Dropper 2 pad was made visible and highlighted, but nothing shows it was ever bought. Either the pad touch path was never exercised or it does not fire for the test character. The acceptance criteria for the pad vanishing and the next pads appearing are therefore unverified.
issues.fix_hint: Confirm the pad Touched handler accepts any character part (resolve the player via `hit:FindFirstAncestorOfClass('Model')` and `Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter`). Make sure the highlighted pad is reachable and not blocked by collision. Add a ForgeTest hook or server-side self-check that simulates a pad touch for the claimed player, so `upgrades_bought` is exercised and bumped in the playtest.

issues.problem: `cubes_dropped` reached 15 within a 32s uptime, with auto-claim after a 20s timeout. At one cube per 2s that should be about 6 cubes, so either the claim happened much earlier than 20s or the drop rate is faster than the spec's 2s. This could mean the claim timing or drop interval does not match the spec.
issues.fix_hint: Log or bump a counter with the claim timestamp. Verify that auto-claim fires at `PlotThemes.CLAIM_TIMEOUT` (20s) after join, and that the dropper interval is 2s at base. If the playtest harness shortens the timeouts, make sure that is intentional and not leaking into normal play.

issues.problem: The player never made the first purchase in the run. tutorial_reshown=1, but upgrades_bought is missing and the census shows beams=0, so nothing strongly leads the player from the plot to the Dropper 2 pad.
issues.fix_hint: Set STUCK_RESHOW_SECONDS to 2 for the buy step (STUCK_RESHOW_BY_STEP[3]=2). Keep the BEAM_WIDTH 3 yellow beam on until upgrades_bought>=1. Change the banner text to 'Step on the glowing pad to buy Dropper 2 ($10)!'.

issues.problem: Cash-in feedback is thin. The census shows sounds=6 but sounds_played=0 and client_sounds_played=0, and cashin_fx_sent never increments, so the batched FX and the coin tick may not be reaching the player.
issues.fix_hint: Play the Coin tick on every collect (or every 2nd cube) via a Sound parented to the collector with PlaybackSpeed from pitchForTier. Increment ForgeTelemetry 'cashin_fx_sent' whenever a batch is sent. Flash the collector Neon yellow for 0.15s and add a sparkle emitter burst of 6 at the intake.

issues.problem: Census bursts=0 and particles=8 for a 764-part world, and the purchase, ore-tier and rebirth big moments have no verified camera shake or FOV punch.
issues.fix_hint: Make sure the burst helper emits at the pad on purchase (30 gold sparkles) and at the dropper for ore tier (shockwave ring tween of Size and Transparency in the gem colour). Call the camera shake: small for purchases, medium plus a FOV 70->80->70 punch for ore tiers, large for rebirth.

issues.problem: The first minute needs several quick wins, but only Dropper 2 at $10 is confirmed reachable. With zero starting cash and $5 cubes every 2s, a stalled player has nothing else to chase.
issues.fix_hint: Keep Dropper 2 at 10, Speed 1 at 20 and Dropper 3 at 40. Add a short toast field to each upgrade, such as 'Unlocked: Dropper 2! Income x2', so every purchase has a clear reward line. Make sure the next pad's cost is visible on its billboard as soon as the previous pad is bought.

issues.problem: The purchase and shop path is unverified in playtest: the upgrades_bought, shop_opened and shop_purchases counters never moved. An insufficient-cash touch gives no visible reaction.
issues.fix_hint: On a pad touch with too little cash, flash the pad Neon red for 0.2s, play the Error buzz and send the toast 'Need $X more'. Rate-limit this per player to 1.5s. Increment 'upgrades_bought' on success, then tween the pad Size to 0 with a Back tween before destroying it.

issues.problem: The plot and plaza look good (0 grey parts, 15 materials, 21 lights), but the plot has no ambient motion to make the world feel alive between purchases.
issues.fix_hint: Add a gentle looping tween to each theme's glow decor (a Neon strip or crystal pulsing Transparency 0 to 0.3 over 1.5s). Add a small ambient ParticleEmitter per theme (fireflies, snow, embers) at low Rate.

iterations.summary: The game runs cleanly with no errors or warnings. The plaza, six themes and map all build, and the player is auto-claimed onto a plot. Cubes drop (15) and are collected (13), and the tutorial, highlight and juice systems fire. The buy flow never ran in the playtest, so the second half of the core loop is unverified.

corrections.note: After a plot is claimed (by the gate or by auto-claim) no cube is ever dropped and Cash stays 0: in the playtest plots_claimed=1 but cubes_dropped never appears. Root cause: claim() calls Tycoon.new(player, entry.plot), which is only a constructor now; nothing calls :start(). Use Tycoon.startPlot(player, entry.plot) (it builds and starts the tycoon and tracks it per plot) and in release() use Tycoon.stopPlot(entry.plot) instead of t:destroy(). Keep everything else as it is.

Every plot logs a warning '[PlotBuilder] buildClaimGate failed: ServerScriptService.PlazaBuilder:246: invalid argument #1 (CFrame expected, got Instance)' (x8), so the themed claim gates are never built and only the plain fallback gate appears. Root cause: PlotBuilder calls plaza.buildClaimGate(model, theme, origin, size, idx) but PlazaBuilder.buildClaimGate(plotCFrame, theme) takes the plot's CFrame first. Call plaza.buildClaimGate(origin, theme) (origin is the plot CFrame). Also only build Config.PLOT_COUNT (6) plots, one per theme: right now 8 plots are built for 6 themes.

There are 6 plot themes but Config says MAX_PLOTS = 8, so Game.server builds 8 plots and two of them repeat a theme. Set MAX_PLOTS = 6 and add PLOT_COUNT = 6. The world floor also looks unfinished: add BASEPLATE_COLOR = Color3.fromRGB(116, 196, 98) (a bright grass green) and BASEPLATE_MATERIAL = Enum.Material.Grass so the builder never leaves the default grey baseplate.

Rebirth never works: the client prints 'RebirthClient: Remotes folder missing' because RebirthService.init() (which creates ReplicatedStorage.Remotes and the rebirth remotes) is never called, nothing requires RebirthService at startup. Require ServerScriptService.RebirthService here and call RebirthService.init() right after UpgradeService.init(), before players are set up. Also the world's Baseplate keeps the default grey: after PlotBuilder.buildBase(), set workspace.Baseplate (if present) Color to Config.BASEPLATE_COLOR and Material to Config.BASEPLATE_MATERIAL when those exist.

In PlotClaimService.luau, use the single real plot table shape that PlotBuilder/PlazaBuilder return and drop the defensive fallbacks. Count plaza_built only once, in PlazaBuilder. One claim function should be the only place that increments plots_claimed and plot_assigned, with an early return on a repeat call. The 20s auto-claim should call it and increment auto_claims once. Verify: gate touch hides the gate, shows the player name on the sign, and starts the Tycoon drop loop. Free the plot when the owner leaves.

Make all pad and shop purchases go through one server function in UpgradeService: reject touches from non-owners, apply a per-player per-upgrade debounce plus an owned flag so the cost is deducted exactly once, do nothing when cash is short, and increment dropper_bought or conveyor_bought on success. Check that Tycoon.luau has no second purchase path. Only the Dropper 2 pad ($10, billboard with name and cost) shows after the claim, and the next pads appear as 'requires' ids are satisfied.

Swarm testers (7 of 10) report: after buying the second dropper the 'LOCKED - buy 2nd Dropper' label and the '$25' legacy pad text never update. These come from the first version of the game: the legacy DropperButton and ConveyorButton pads and the LockLabel on Dropper2 are still built here, next to the real UpgradeService buy pads, so players see two purchase systems that disagree. Remove the legacy DropperButton/ConveyorButton pads and the LockLabel from buildPlot (return nil for those fields, keep every other field the same) so UpgradeService pads are the only way to buy. Also, nothing stops players at the baseplate edge, so they walk off and die: in buildBase, add 4 invisible, anchored, CanCollide walls 40 studs tall just inside the baseplate edge, plus a low visible hedge (Grass material, dark green, 3 studs tall) along the same line.

The old hint line ('Next: Dropper 25 (have N)' / 'Dropper affordable! AI testers (2 rounds) pressed Buy on the Gold Ore and Cash x1.5 cards with 464-1.2K cash and nothing happened (fired=false). The shop also showed different owned states from the pads and HUD. Root cause: ownedSet is only refreshed when the panel opens or a shop purchase replies. Upgrades bought on the world pads (UpgradeBought remote, fired for every purchase) and the rebirth reset never reach it, so after buying Silver Ore on a pad the shop still thinks Silver is missing, shows Gold as Locked, and tryBuy returns early without asking the server. Fix: (1) listen to the UpgradeBought remote and add the id to ownedSet, then refresh(); (2) re-request the owned list (syncRemote:FireServer()) on rebirth and whenever Cash drops sharply; (3) in tryBuy, never block on the client's view of requires. The server is the authority, so fire buyRemote and show buyFail only when the server refuses or does not answer.

Two tutorial systems run at once and fight over the banner. Stop firing this module's own step events and stop bumping tutorial_steps here.

The stuck re-show is spam: STUCK_SECONDS falls back to TutorialConfig.STUCK_RESHOW_SECONDS = 5, so the banner re-pops every 5 seconds (tutorial_reshown 70-130 per round), and the guide never goes away. Re-show at most every 15 seconds (use math.max(15, STUCK_SECONDS)), and once 60 seconds have passed since the player's tutorial started, finish it: publish the final step, clear the beam and target, and stop updating that player.
